title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
The government, trade unions, universities, associations, cooperatives, and self-help groups adopted and implemented an activity-based learning approach for enterprise development which aimed to advance innovation, productivity, and sustainability of 10,709 youth and start-up business owners. During the Cambodia Entrepreneurship Day in September 2022, the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports (MoEYS) promoted entrepreneurship training and business idea competition which benefited 4887 youth in all 25 provinces, to obtain basic knowledge and skills to start businesses and soft skills for future career development. The event attained high public interest with over 65,000 social media viewers and various TV, radio, and online media picked up the event. AISEC and the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports operationalized ILO’s Ready-for-Business training module which promoted the leadership and soft skills of over 100 youth AIESEC members during the November 2022 Asia Pacific Leadership Summit. JILAF, and CPSA (local non-profit organization), implemented the Our COOP training programme which benefitted 604 people, including farmers and cooperative members, advancing their understanding of cooperatives principles and structure. With funding from the Governments of Japan and Switzerland, the ILO delivered technical assistance to the Ministry of Education, Youth, and Sports to organize Cambodia Entrepreneurship Day 2022. The ILO provided a training tool on entrepreneurship as well as advice on the coordination of the event.
With DC funding from the Governments of Japan and Switzerland, the ILO built the capacity of constituents and social partners to deliver activity-based learning training. Benefited organizations include the Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Tourism, informal workers group, YEAC, CWEA, CPSA, GIZ Cambodia, IOM Cambodia, and various international and local NGOs.
The ILO provided technical expertise on entrepreneurship and SME development to a local community of entrepreneurship-supporting organization - the Entrepreneurship Ecosystem Builders Network, initiated by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, USAID, and Pact Cambodia. The ILO participated in Cambodia’s Ecosystem Strengthening Conference (CAMESCO) in 2022 and promoted the importance of SMEs and entrepreneurship through peer support.
